rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest to violating: chunk 2 "Prework" line 10: "...for the two-session compare, and [long-running shapes]..." — "the two-session compare" is a definite-article compound naming an activity not yet introduced anywhere earlier in the deck (Big Idea, chunk 1, doesn't mention sessions). It stays inside because the phrase is self-descriptive on its own words (compare across two sessions) and the sentence's actionable content (find transcripts, at this anchor) doesn't depend on the reader already knowing M6's specific two-session conceit; this exact line is unchanged by the pinned diff and was independently re-verified this session (`grep -n '^## 25\|^## 17' reference/claude-code-for-engineers.md` -> both anchors resolve). Second-closest: chunk 4 line 25 "gaps the three-pattern didn't anticipate" — verified this session as arc-earned, not a fresh coinage: `learn-from-the-test.md` lines 179/228/244 show the term is deliberately earned in M5's closing lecture ("Ronacher's three-pattern... Earns its name in the closing lecture, not before"), so M6 reusing it without re-defining is the spine-vocabulary carve-out working as designed, confirmed again in-file at chunk 6 line 56 where the elaboration lands. Chunk 8 line 74 "the lens you built" is likewise arc-earned: `curriculum/lectures/reading-the-return.md` (M5's in-room opener per `learn-from-the-test.md` line 168) states in its own body, above its maintainer cut, "Practitioners hit the same three. Use them as lenses, not boxes" (line 11) — "lens" is established M5 vocabulary for the diagnostic frame, not a cold metaphor. Chunk 5 line 41 "the exercise's gap map and stack-map" resolves under the session-artifact carve-out (the exercise is linked at chunk 4 line 37, directly before Human close in deck order). All three renamed include-links (chunk 4 line 31, chunk 4 line 37, chunk 5 line 49) now read as titles, verified against each target's actual H1 this session (`the-2-frontiers.md` -> "# The 2 frontiers of learning", `exercises/spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md` -> "# Map the gaps, read your stack", `the-loop-has-a-name.md` -> "# The check you built is an eval") — all three now match exactly, so no title/target drift and no orphaned referent.

Closest: chunk 8 line 76 "The training opened on a trick." — sums the whole training's arc by content (a closer doing its job, the rule's own carve-out), not by file position (doesn't say "the opening lecture" or name a module number); the training's opening "trick" isn't unpacked in the same sentence, matching the given PASS example ("The story of building this training is the shape you just ran") in that both trade specificity for closing-beat compression, which the carve-out explicitly allows for a terminal-module closer. Chunk 2 line 10's two lookup-page links are navigational, named by title/section, exempt under §2's carve-out — re-verified live this session (both reference anchors resolve). All 8 structural include-links (chunks 4, 5, 8) name their target document in the link text (never by position) and are out of §2's scope by the rule's own text regardless.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Full bold inventory this session (`grep -n '\*\*'` on body): chunk 3's six LO bullets are the architecture-mandated `- **[verb]** [thing]` template, N/A by rule text. Chunk 5 line 45 "**Self-study variant.**" and chunk 8 line 78 "**Going deeper:**" are single two-word mode-labels, well inside the handle cap, one per chunk. Chunk 4 carries two bold leads (line 27 "**Packaged session thin or missing?**", 5 words; line 29 "**Just can't get the M5 session working?**", 7 words) — this is the genuine boundary case: taken as whole-sentence bold leads they would exceed both the ≤1-per-slide budget and (for the second) the ≲5-word handle cap, and the maintainer's line-97 accept-note that covers this passage is scoped to `check_student_facing.md` §5 (golden-path-only-in-body), not to §9's emphasis budget — it does not actually authorize the bold spend. Judged PASS on the merits instead: the two blockquotes function as a scanned troubleshooting menu ("if your session is in state A, do X; if state B, do Y") rather than linear narrative, which is the functional shape §9's own reading-list/menu carve-out describes (bold as navigational mode-marker, budget off, handle cap still roughly held at 5-7 words for a question-form label). Flagged as a TODO below since the existing accept-note doesn't name this rule and a future judge could reasonably read it the other way.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Unnumbered trailing clause: "`## Next` is two plain sentences: what the next module does, what the student carries into it (Antti 2026-08-14)."
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm the clause prevents: a closer that teaches steals the slide it points at. M6 is the terminal module of the AE101 core arc, so there is no next module's beat to front-run — the front-running concern is structurally moot here. Chunk 8 (lines 72-83) runs longer than two sentences (task/lens sentence, loop-not-sending sentence, "It's yours now", arc-closing pair, Going-deeper aside, capstone sign-off), but the actual BANS the clause enforces are clean: no mechanism aside in parentheses, no housekeeping line, no term a later module coins (there is no later module). The capstone sign-off is separately authorized by the maintainer accept-note at line 93 (exception to `check_writing.md` §6). Content-type is the operative test per the rule's own text, not a literal sentence count, and the corpus reads it the same way elsewhere.
